F000.text: CONSTRUCTED COUNTEREXAMPLES — not an actual policy.

F001.text: For library lending, an access record (AR) means the dated entry of a visitor's permission to borrow.

F002.text: An access record is not an annual report.

F003.text: For finance reporting, an annual report (AR) means the signed yearly account of spending.

F004.text: In the following finance rules, AR always means annual report.

F005.text: You must sign and date the AR before submitting it.

F006.text: Signing and dating are both required.

F007.text: Visitors do not need an access record for a public tour, and librarians do not need an access record to enter the archive.

F008.text: These are separate exemptions for different activities.

F009.text: If an access record is lost and remains unreported for more than a month, staff must request a replacement.

F010.text: If travel is imminent, a temporary pass may be issued.

F011.text: Finance reviewers should check the AR for missing pages.

F012.text: Missing pages may indicate an incomplete submission.

F013.text: An annual report must not be altered without the director's approval.

F014.text: The director approves alterations; this sentence does not identify who would perform an alteration.

F015.text: Staff must file the access record.

F016.text: Staff must retain the access record for two years.
